# Dia — The Cut

## #0 — Begin inside the field

A discrimination requires something to distinguish, a criterion and a field within which the distinction matters. Dia names contrast, exclusion, orientation and selection. [C50](../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C50-Dia-Syn.md) gives the productive cut its full office before distinguishing severance. The [core spine, §IV](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) works the change from held polarity to cancellation and appropriation.

The input `(-1)/(+1)` retains zero as an axis of direction. Both poles have determinate signs; neither sign independently produces the axis that makes it positive or negative.

## #1 — Make a selection precise

Let a finite set contain two labelled alternatives `a,b`, and let a stated criterion select `a`. The output is exact relative to the input and criterion. The unselected `b` is an excluded alternative in this selection; the selection alone says nothing about its availability under a different criterion.

This elementary construction exhibits productive Dia. A distinction acquires local force by specifying its domain. Proof, measurement, criticism and decision need that force. Treating an excluded alternative as nonexistent in every possible account adds a claim the selection did not establish.

## #2 — Change the operator

The core's arithmetic carriers are three different operations:

`(-1)+(+1)=0`,

`(-1)-(+1)=−2`,

`(+1)-(-1)=+2`.

Addition cancels the values. Directed subtraction measures the entire span from one pole or the other, with the result's sign depending on orientation. The subtraction results are not one ambiguous `±2`: each has an exact calculation. In each case the operator has changed from a retained polar relation to a scalar result.

## #3 — Identify what the result omits

A zero sum does not retain the identities of its summands. Many pairs sum to zero. Similarly, a difference of 2 by itself does not retain the two original endpoints: `(1,−1)` and `(4,2)` have the same difference. These are demonstrable losses of information in the specified maps.

The native reading places cancellation and appropriation here. Cancellation lets a scalar terminus stand for the relation; appropriation lets a pole present the whole span as its own. The arithmetic supports that formal distinction. A psychic or political judgement requires the actual case's source, agency and consequences; the equation does not decide those by itself.

## #4 — Preserve the cut's conditions

A returned selection retains the input alternatives, criterion, chosen result and effects of exclusion. This is a present operational example of [Syn's](syn.md) gathering discipline. Recombination does not require equalising unequal claims. It makes the chosen result answerable to the conditions under which it was chosen.

The [two temporal readings](chronic.md) can each contain productive or severing cuts. A current map can expose its exclusions; a historical sequence can conceal its inherited field. Synchronic and diachronic therefore do not classify the ethical or logical quality of a cut.

## #5→0 — Give the result a return route

The output is a distinction that can be used and reconsidered without losing its exactness. Its return asks what remains excluded, what changed in the field, and whether another criterion is now warranted. Dia's local edge persists within the gathering that makes another operation possible.

This record returns-to [A13](../../../section-rooms/arguments/A13-Two-Logics-of-Two-Dia-Syn.md) and [C50](../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C50-Dia-Syn.md). The [Sheffer stroke](../formal-neighbours/sheffer-stroke.md) has a distinct Boolean signature; its functional completeness supplies no automatic proof of the native AND/OR stroke.
